#### Use Grok Bot

# Add a Bot to Your Meetings

A Bot can join your Google Meet, Zoom, or Microsoft Teams calls. It listens,
takes notes, answers questions in the meeting chat, and sends you a summary and
action items when the call ends.

Meetings are available on Team, Enterprise, and Ultra plans. Enterprise admins
can turn on Meetings in settings. See [Can a Team Bot join meetings?](#can-a-team-bot-join-meetings)

## How do I add a Bot to a meeting?

1. Paste the Google Meet, Zoom, or Microsoft Teams link into your chat with the
   Bot, and ask it to join and take notes.
2. Approve the card when the Bot asks.
3. When the meeting starts, the host admits the Bot. It joins as **Bot name
   (your first name's Bot) - transcribing**, or **Bot name (Team Bot) -
   transcribing** for a Team Bot.

A Bot that follows your calendar can also join scheduled meetings on its own.

Not sure what to ask? Open the Bot's details. If it hasn't joined a meeting
before, **Add to meeting** under **Suggested** drafts a question asking the Bot
how to add it to meetings.

## How do I manage a Bot's upcoming meetings?

Open the Bot's details. Meetings it's joining or attending appear under
**Upcoming**, with a countdown to the join time, the next join time for a
scheduled meeting, or **Taking notes** while it's in the call.

Hover a meeting you scheduled and open its menu to see **Meeting actions**:

* **Disable Interactivity** keeps the Bot listening and taking notes, without
  answering in the meeting. The row shows **Muted**. While the meeting is still
  scheduled, **Enable Interactivity** turns it back on. Once the Bot is joining
  or in the call, quit and add it again to turn it back on.
* **Cancel** removes a scheduled meeting.
* **Quit** takes the Bot out of a meeting it's joining or attending.

## How do I talk to a Bot during a meeting?

Address the Bot by name in the meeting chat, and it answers there.

* **Zoom private chat.** A private chat message to the Bot gets a private
  answer.
* **Conference rooms.** A request from a conference room device counts as
  coming from the room, not one person.

If someone in the meeting asks for something the Bot held back, the Bot tells
you who asked and offers to send it. It won't share your credentials in a
meeting.

## What happens after a meeting?

When the call ends, the Bot sends a summary and action items in its chat. If you
have [Pages](/grok-bot/files-and-results#pages), a longer report goes on a page,
with the link in the chat. Ask the Bot anytime for the summary or transcript of
a past meeting.

Meetings use the settings of the person who started them.

## Can a Team Bot join meetings?

Yes, when its team allows meetings. On Enterprise plans, admins turn
meetings on or off for everyone's Bots with **Meetings** under **Bot
Capabilities** on the Grok Bot page of the team dashboard. When it's off, Bots
can't join or read meetings, and a Bot that was scheduled to join tells you
meetings are no longer available. See [Grok Bot for
teams and enterprises](/grok-bot/teams-and-enterprises#meetings).
